Instead of complex menus and unnecessary features, Homer offers a clear, minimal interface focused on one thing: easy audiobook and podcast playback. Use the special "lockdown mode" to turn an Android tablet into a dedicated, single-purpose audiobook and podcast device. Designed for: - Elderly who want simple, independent listening - Visually impaired users who benefit from large controls and spoken titles - Non-tech-savvy users who find standard apps overwhelming - People with cognitive challenges who need basic functionality Easy to use: - Large, easy-to-tap buttons - Simple navigation with swipe left/right - Flat content structure (no deep nested folders) - No ads, no pop-ups, no distracting clutter - Optional title read-aloud for accessibility - Flip-to-stop: place device screen-down to pause playback Lockdown mode: - only playback functionality - blocks exiting the app - hides settings - no access to other apps, notifications nor settings Audiobooks: - Play DRM-free audiobooks from device storage - Resume position saved separately for each book Podcasts: - Automatically updates to show the latest 1-5 episodes - Downloads full episodes for reliable offline playback Caregiver-managed setup (secondary role): - A caregiver configures content and settings in advance - Optional lockdown mode hides all apps and functionality except the player - Device is prepared once, then used independently by the listener Additional features: - High-contrast light and dark themes - Customizable controls: volume, chapter skip, forward, rewind - Adjustable playback speed - Sleep timer with shake-to-continue How it works: 1. Install Homer on an Android 7+ phone or tablet. 2. Add audiobooks/podcasts and adjust the interface as needed. 3. Optionally lock or hide settings. 4. Hand the device to the listener for simple, independent daily use. Homer makes audiobook and podcast listening accessible for people who cannot comfortably use standard smartphone apps.

name: Super Productivity
short: Free to do list & time tracker
description: Organize your daily tasks at one place while making time tracking a lot less annoying. Super Productivity is a ToDo List / Time Tracker / Personal Jira Task Manager for multiple platforms. Features Plan, track & summarize . Create time sheets and work summaries in a breeze to easily export them to your companies time tracking system. Integrate with Jira , Github and Gitlab . Auto import tasks assigned to you, plan the details locally, automatically create worklogs and get notified right away, when somfething changes. Organize your project's data. Create notes , attach files or create bookmarks for links, files and even commands and have it all out of the way, once you're ready for the weekend. Helps you to establish healthy habits . A break timer reminds to you, when it's time to step away. You also can collect personal metrics for yourself to see, which of your work routines need adjustments. Stuck and procrastinating? No problem! Super Productivity's anti procrastination feature helps you to reconsider your options and a pomodoro timer is also always at hand. Super Productivity does NOT actively collect any data and there are no user accounts or registration. It's free and open-source and always will be. NOTE: There will however be data loaded from app.super-productivity.com on app start and if you use one of the third party providers, you will have to comply with their private policy. Private Policy

name: Camera Date Folders
short: Sort photos from camera folder into a date specific subfolder structure
description: Sorts all photos, located in the device's camera folder, into a date specific subfolder structure. This makes it easier to transfer specific photos to a computer, e.g. via USB cable (MTP protocol). Either keep photos inside the camera folder tree or move or copy them to a separate directory. This can also be used as a simple backup method. Up to three levels are supported: year, month and day. The sorting can be reverted, i.e. all photos can be moved back to the base directory (but not back to the camera directory in case a destination directory is specified). On the demand a file name prefix like "IMG_" or "PXL_" can be appended instead or completely removed. Note that this operation is not revertible. The program does not read metadata (EXIF) from the photo files, instead it uses the data information encoded in the filenames. To meet Google's restrictive policy, the Play Store variant of the program must use Google's proprietary Storage Access Framework when running on Android 11 or newer. As a consequence, file operations are extremely slow. This restriction partially exists also for older Android versions and not at all for the F-Droid version of the program. In this case standard file access calls can be activated alternatively, which accelerate the file operations with a factor of approximately 90 (!).

name: Simple Nextcloud
short: A small Nextcloud file browser without a duplicate upload cache
description: Simple Nextcloud is a deliberately small client for accessing files on your own Nextcloud server. Features: * Browse folders and view images. * Upload and download files or complete folders. * Move, copy, rename, create, and delete files and folders. * Share files with Nextcloud users or create public links. * Send files to Nextcloud from Android's share sheet. * Use Nextcloud as a storage provider in Android's system file picker. Unlike the official Nextcloud client, Simple Nextcloud does not keep a second, hidden copy of every uploaded file. It only caches folder metadata and image previews to make browsing more responsive. The app connects directly to the Nextcloud server you configure. It contains no advertising, analytics, or tracking.

name: MakeACopy
short: Privacy-focused document scanner with OCR and PDF export
description: MakeACopy is an open-source document scanner app for Android that allows you to digitize paper documents with offline OCR functionality. The app is privacy-friendly and works completely offline — no cloud connection, no tracking. Features: • Camera scanning: Capture documents using your device’s camera • Edge detection: Automatic document boundary detection using OpenCV, enhanced by a custom-trained ONNX inference model • Perspective correction: Manually or automatically adjust document perspective • Grayscale export: Optional grayscale filter applied during PDF creation • OCR: Offline text recognition using PaddleOCR in the published paddle flavor • PDF export: Save scanned documents as searchable PDFs • Share & save: Export locally or share via other apps • Dark mode: System-based Material 3 theme with light and dark appearance • Privacy-focused: Fully offline — no data leaves your device The F-Droid and Google Play listings provide the paddle flavor with PaddleOCR. The standard flavor with Tesseract remains available through GitHub Releases for users who still need Tesseract language data or workflows. MakeACopy is F-Droid compliant and builds native libraries from source during the build process, ensuring that no prebuilt binaries are included in the repository. All components are open source and respect your privacy. MakeACopy is free and open source. If you find it useful, please consider supporting development: https://ko-fi.com/egdels License: Apache License 2.0

name: URSA
short: Native Android client for Uptime Kuma with FOSS push, no Google services.
description: URSA keeps every self-hosted Uptime Kuma monitor a glance away on your phone. Connect directly to your server for live state, incident context, management, and private push without an account, analytics, Google services, or a paid relay. Features: * Live monitor state, response-time trends, uptime, heartbeat history, and TLS certificate detail. * Incident, certificate, domain, event, 30-day aggregate, and pinned-live fleet views for fast triage. * Search, quick filters, advanced filters, saved views, favourites, groups, tags, compact rows, and responsive tablet layouts. * Multiple encrypted server connections with password/TOTP or imported sessions, optional self-signed TLS, and up to eight custom access headers for Pangolin, Cloudflare Access, and similar reverse proxies. * Create and safely edit common monitor settings, including SFTP password or private-key access, assign notification providers, manage groups/tags, run confirmed bulk pause/resume, and manage maintenance. * UnifiedPush alerts through a distributor you choose, including per-monitor modes, severity, quiet hours, delays, repeats, acknowledge/snooze, and managed Kuma setup. * Slow-response and certificate-expiry alerts generated locally on your device. * Public status pages with native groups, uptime, recent checks, maintenance, and incident history. * Encrypted portable backups, encrypted offline cache, optional biometric/device credential lock, and sensitive screens protected in release builds. * Native Android extras: widget, Quick Settings tile, shortcuts, scoped deep links, notification actions, and an opt-in always-on glance display. * Light/dark mode with Kuma status colors and optional Material You. * Optional manual check for stable releases from URSA's official GitHub repository. A separate Wear OS APK is available from GitHub Releases with a standalone public dashboard, detail view, tile, complications, and optional same-signed phone pairing for private monitor actions. The F-Droid phone build remains free of Play Services. URSA is free and open source with no ads, tracking, premium tier, or subscription. It is an independent client and is not affiliated with Uptime Kuma.

name: CipherNotes
short: Notes. Encrypted. Local. Nothing more.
description: Cipher is a privacy-first notes app with AES-256-GCM encryption. All data stays on your device. Zero cloud, zero telemetry. Features: - Text notes & checklists - Per-note password encryption - Offline-only - Open source (MIT)

name: Shopping List Calculator
short: Plan your grocery trips, add up costs, and keep track of your budget.
description: Shopping List Calculator helps you plan grocery trips and see what you're spending as you shop. Make your list, enter prices as you go, and keep track of your total before you reach the checkout. Set a budget to see how much you have left to spend, include sales tax, and save your regular shopping lists to use again next time. Features: • Create shopping lists and arrange items in the order you shop • Check off items as you go and easily make changes • See your running total, including sales tax • Set a shopping budget and track how much is left • Calculate costs for multiple items or items sold by weight • Save, name, and edit reusable shopping lists • Add a saved list to your current trip or start fresh with it • Clear prices and checkmarks while keeping your list for another trip • Choose your currency and how prices are displayed • Enter prices quickly and choose whether to enter the item name or price first • Shop with a dark interface • Use the app offline, with no account, ads, or tracking Saved lists remember item names, so you can enter fresh prices and quantities each trip. Your lists and settings stay on your device.

name: Linthra
short: Open-source, local-first music player for music you own. No forced sync.
description: Linthra is an open-source Android music player for people who keep their music on their own devices or self-hosted servers. It plays local files, and it streams from self-hosted music servers such as Jellyfin and Navidrome/Subsonic — you bring your own server and sign in with your own account. Linthra is an unofficial community client. It is not affiliated with Jellyfin, Navidrome, or Subsonic. The app is still early alpha. It's usable for testing on a real device, but it isn't production-stable and has a few rough edges. The lists below separate what works today from what's still planned. On privacy: * No ads, no tracking, no analytics, and no crash-reporting or telemetry SDK. * No account to create, and nothing phones home — streaming is the default, and downloads only happen when you ask for them (Wi-Fi only unless you opt in to mobile data). * When you sign in to a server, the password is used once to get a session token, then dropped; the token is stored encrypted and never logged. * Open-source under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later, so anyone can read, build, and contribute to it. What works today: * Local library — pick a folder with the Storage Access Framework (no broad storage permission), scan it, and browse Songs, Albums, and Artists with search. * Streaming from your own Jellyfin or Navidrome / Subsonic server: test the connection, sign in, sync, and play, including over HTTPS. * A smart offline cache — download tracks for offline play, with a size limit and a "Keep offline" pin. * Queue / Up Next, playlists and favourites (synced with Jellyfin where it's supported), and automatic "smart mixes" built from on-device signals. * Background playback with a media notification and lock-screen, Bluetooth, and wired-headset controls, plus shuffle / repeat and synced lyrics. * Android Auto browsing, and casting to a Chromecast, speaker, or TV through a pure-Dart Cast implementation (no Google Play Services). Still to come: * Reading tags and album art from local files (for now they show file names). * Subsonic favourites, lyrics, and cover art, and fuller playlist sync. * "Download all" for an album or playlist. * More sources, such as WebDAV / NAS, behind the same interface. * A Linux desktop build later, from the same codebase. Linthra is distributed for testing as a sideloaded APK from GitHub Releases. It isn't on F-Droid or Google Play yet.

name: TimeLimit.io
short: Flexibly limit the usage duration
description: Flexible Apps are grouped to categories (a category can contain one or multiple App). You can chose per category at which times it should be allowed. This allows preventing playing games too late. Additionally, you can configure time limit rules. These rules limit the total usage duration at one day or over multiple days (e.g. a weekend). It is possible to combine both, e.g. 2 hours per week end day, but in total only 3 hours. Moreover, there is the possibility to set an extra time. This allows using something longer than regulary once. This can be used as bonus. There is additionally the option to disable all time limits temporarily (e.g. for the whole day or an hour). Multi user support There is the scenario that one device is used by exactly one user. However, with tablets, there are often multiple possible users. Due to that, it is possible to create multiple user profiles in TimeLimit. Each user has got different settings and time counters. There are two kinds of users: parents and children. If a parent was chosen as user, then there are no restrictions. Parents can chose any other user as current user. Children can only chose themselves as current user. Multi device support There are scenarios in which one user has got multiple devices. Instead of time limits per device and splitting the limits across the devices, it is possible to assign one user to multiple devices. Then the usage durations are counted together and allowing an App automatically affects all devices. Depending on the settings, only one device per time can be used or multiple devices at the same time. However, un the second case, it is possible to use more time than available e.g. at connection interruptions. Connected It is possible to view and change settings from any linked device. This connection is possible - if wanted - using your server. Notes Some features cost money if you don't use your own server. These features cost 1 € per month/ 10 € per year (in Germany). TimeLimit does not work good at some smartphone brands (mostly Huawei and Wiko). With the correct settings, it can work better. But better is not good. If it "does not work": This can be caused by power saving features. You can find at https://dontkillmyapp.com/ how you can disable these features. Get in touch with the support if that does not help. TimeLimit uses the permission for the usage stats access. This is only used to detect the currently used App. Based on the currently used App, the App is blocked, allowed,

name: WhisperType Keyboard
short: Offline Android keyboard with QWERTY typing and on-device speech dictation
description: WhisperType is a full Android input method (IME) with a real QWERTY keyboard plus offline voice dictation. Unlike dictation-only "keyboards" that only show a microphone button, WhisperType lets you type normally and use speech when you want. Features: - Full QWERTY layout with numbers, symbols, and a categorized emoji picker - Shift / caps lock, sentence caps, double-space period, word-delete swipe - On-device word suggestions and clipboard history - Long-press accents and extra symbols - Microphone key for offline on-device speech-to-text (25s warning, 30s auto-stop) - Downloadable Whisper models: tiny.en, base.en (default), or small.en (int8) - Import your own sherpa-onnx Whisper zip - No API keys - audio, clipboard, and learned words stay on your device - Free and open source (MIT) Setup: 1. Install WhisperType 2. Enable it in system keyboard settings 3. Select it as the input method 4. Grant microphone permission 5. Download or import a speech model in settings 6. Type or tap the mic to dictate On-device recognition uses sherpa-onnx (includes ONNX Runtime). Whisper models download on demand from Hugging Face when the user chooses Download; Import works offline.

name: Relagent
short: Trustworthy AI assistant that runs 100% on your hardware
description: Relagent is a private and selfhosted AI assistant that runs on your hardware. In addition to this app, you need to run the Relagent engine. To get started, please have a look at the project's readme at https://gitlab.com/RmMsr/relagent. The goal of the Relagent project is an accessible solution for agentic AI services with full control over your data. Setting up your own installation should be within reach without considerable technical knowledge or financial investment. The software is designed to be resource-efficient without any hidden costs. What Relagent brings you: * 🗨️ Chat interface : Chat with your AI assistant and manage sessions. * 🌐 Persistent sessions : Open new sessions and continue them on any device. Data stays on your systems only. * 🎤 Speech Integration : Input and Output on-device with about 40 languages. * ⚖️ Use any open-weights model : By using the OpenAI-compatible chat completions protocol, you can choose the inference service that works best for you. No external service is needed - but you can use one. * 🔒️ API Key Authentication : Restrict access to your data. Combine with an HTTPS proxy or a VPN to protect your data while accessing it from anywhere. * 🧰 Agentic tools : For example, web search. You can decide in which cases you want to be asked for permission based on your selected privacy level. What you do NOT need : * Register for a third-party service (unless you want to use a commercial LLM provider) * Pay for any usage or access (but I appreciate donations) * Fear that your data ends up in big data silos or model training What you CAN do : * Host the Relagent engine yourself (start on your computer, switch to permanent installation when you are ready) * Run a Large Language Model yourself (needs one additional app, there are several free options with or without a graphical interface to choose from) * Protect the API with HTTPS, Basic Auth or using a VPN. Permissions on your device: * In order to send data between the app and the engine and to download speech models, internet access is needed * For the voice input (ASR) and output (TTS) features several permissions includiing bluetooth and background processing are required. Relagent won't continuously listen on the microphone unless you explicitly activate it For more information: * Find the Relagent source code at https://gitlab.com/RmMsr/relagent. * Have a look at the related Blog at https://venkado.org/. * Follow the author @guesser (https://sigmoid.social/@guesser)

name: Cirrus
short: Weather and rain radar for any location - worldwide
description: Weather and rain radar for any location - worldwide Weather data is provided via the free API from Open-Meteo.com and LibreWXR. Features: - Current weather - Hourly forecasts for up to 16 days - Rain radar - Widget with optional GPS auto position update - No advertisement Minimum permissions: Cirrus only requires the minimum amount of permission, namely only the INTERNET permission. This permission is necessary to make HTTP requests to remote servers for retrieving weather data. Optional: authorization for GPS.

name: Flashy
short: Simple and Privacy-Friendly Flashlight App
description: Handy bright flashlight anytime and anywhere you need it. Practical screen flashlight app using your phone or tablet screen-light or camera-flash. 🔦 Simple and handy Power-saving multi-functional design. Elegant user-friendly flashlight brightness in your pocket. This screen torch light gives brings clarity and sets the mood at the press of a button. ☀️ Control and adjust brightness Customize brightness and screen-color to suit your preferences with this minimalistic flashlight. Rotate the brightness circle and adjust it as per your needs. Setting it lower allows extended use without damaging your device. 🚫 Libre software and no ads This mobile flashlight is privacy-friendly. Perfect choice for users with a device that doesn’t have a camera or broken flashlight. Your safety is guaranteed and it is ad-free, so you won’t be interrupted using it. 💡 Features * Easy to use and privacy-friendly. * No ads. * Elegant and simple design with different themes. * Uses your screen’s light or camera flash as a light-source. * Control and customize the brightness.

name: ADB Captain
short: Run ADB commands on your phone. No root, no PC — via Shizuku.
description: ADB Captain runs ADB commands right on your phone. No computer, no root - it works through Shizuku. What's inside: - Terminal. pm, am, dumpsys, settings, input - anything adb shell takes. Autocomplete pulls from your command history. - Apps. Every installed package in one list, user and system apps separated. Each one gets a plain safety rating, so you know what's safe to disable or remove. - Devices. Model, Android version, battery, connection status. Reboot and screenshots from the same screen. - Logcat. Live system log, filterable by level and text. - Sideload and tools. Install an APK from storage, record the screen, flip Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or airplane mode, type text, open links. AGPL-3.0. No ads, no analytics, no accounts.

name: Immich
short: This is a client app for the self-hostable Immich Server
description: This is a client app for the self-hostable Immich Server (which can be found with the app's source repo). You will need to run/manage the server on your own in order to use the app. Once set up, this app can be used as photo and video backup solution directly from your mobile phone. Features: * Upload and view assets(videos/images). * Multi-user supported. * Quick navigation with drag scroll bar. * Auto Backup. * Support HEIC/HEIF Backup. * Extract and display EXIF info. * Real-time render from multi-device upload event. * Image Tagging/Classification based on ImageNet dataset * Object detection based on COCO SSD. * Search assets based on tags and exif data (lens, make, model, orientation) * Upload assets from your local computer/server using immich cli tools * Reverse geocoding from image exif data * Show asset's location information on map (OpenStreetMap). * Show curated places on the search page * Show curated objects on the search page

name: Gridlink Mail
short: A fast, private JMAP and IMAP email client. No ads, no tracking, no Google.
description: Gridlink Mail is an email client built for JMAP, the modern successor to IMAP. It syncs faster, uses less battery and less data, and was designed for phones rather than adapted to them. It speaks classic IMAP and SMTP too, so it works with any standard mail provider. There is no Gridlink account and no Gridlink server. The app talks only to the mail server you configure. It collects nothing, contains no ads, no tracking and no Google libraries, and it is free software under the GPLv3. Features * JMAP mail, with IMAP/SMTP as a fully supported alternative * Contacts and calendar over JMAP, with CardDAV and CalDAV fallback * Autodiscovery: type your address and let it find the server, or pick the protocol yourself * Remote images blocked by default, so a message cannot phone home unless you let it * OpenPGP support * Self-hosted friendly, including servers using a self-signed certificate * Two-pane layout on unfolded and tablet-sized screens * Swipe actions, undo send, scheduled send and threaded conversations A note on this build Gridlink Mail is a fork of Sterna Mail by emon (https://codeberg.org/emon/sterna-mail), reused under the GPLv3. The mail engine, sync layer and OpenPGP support are emon's work; this fork rebuilds the front end and the setup flow. It is not an official Sterna release and emon does not support it. If you want the original, upstream is the better-tested and actively maintained app.

name: QuorumPony
short: Split a secret into printable cards. Any K of N recover it. Fully offline.
description: QuorumPony splits a secret — an age or GPG key, a seed phrase, a password — into N shares using Shamir's Secret Sharing over GF(2^8). Any K shares reconstruct the secret; any K−1 reveal nothing about it. Each share becomes a printable card with a QR code and a hand-typeable code (Crockford base32, so 0/O and 1/I/L can't be confused). Export all cards as a PDF, print them, and hand them to people or places you trust. Features: • Split a secret from text or a file into 2–16 cards with a chosen threshold • Recover by scanning QR codes with the camera, or typing codes by hand • Check cards: verify a card is intact and part of a backup, without reconstructing the secret • Two-layer integrity: a per-card checksum catches damaged or mistyped cards instantly; an envelope hash confirms the recovered secret is exactly what was backed up • Printable PDF of all cards • Optional biometric/device-credential lock • Six languages: English, Español, Deutsch, Français, 日本語, Português (Brasil) Fully offline: no network permission, no analytics, no accounts. The cryptographic core is open source and pinned byte-for-byte to cross-implementation test vectors shared with the iOS app and a Python reference implementation.

name: Rhythm
short: Your Music, Your Rhythm - Privacy-first player with Material 3 design.
description: Your Music, Your Rhythm Experience your music collection like never before. Rhythm is a beautiful, open-source Material You music player built for audiophiles, supporting both local and streaming playback. Enjoy high-quality audio with zero tracking and absolutely no ads. 🔊 Audiophile-Grade Sound • High-Res Audio: Preserves native sample rates and bit depths for pure, unaltered sound. • Advanced EQ: Perfect your audio with a 10-band equalizer and over 6,000 AutoEQ presets tailored to your specific headphones. • Premium Playback: Enjoy true gapless playback and support for all major formats (FLAC, ALAC, Opus, WAV, MP3, OGG, and Dolby Atmos/EAC3-JOC). 🎨 Gorgeous Material 3 Design • Dynamic Colors: The app's theme adapts beautifully to your wallpaper (Android 12+) and the current album artwork. • Fluid UI: Experience expressive shapes, smooth animations, and an immersive, distraction-free lyrics view. • Responsive Widgets: Control your music straight from your home screen with modern Material 3 layouts. 📚 Smart Library & Lyrics • Dual-Mode Playback: Seamlessly switch between your local music library and streaming servers (Subsonic, Navidrome, Jellyfin). • Synced Lyrics: Sing along with word-by-word highlighting via LRCLib, or use the local editor for custom offsets. • Ultimate Organization: Browse by Songs, Liked, Playlists, Albums, Artists, Album Artists, Dates, or the folder Explorer. • Multi-Select Power: Manage your queue, share, or delete multiple tracks at once with batch actions. • Reliable Scanning: A full-scan media scanner ensures no songs are ever missed, with configurable allowed formats. ⚙️ Feature-Packed • Rhythm Guard: Integrated hearing safety system with age-aware volume protection. • Built-in metadata editor with artwork integration from Deezer and YouTube Music. • Sleep timer, playback statistics, and stability tools for a crash-free experience. • Easy queue management and M3U playlist import/export. • In-app auto-updates directly from GitHub. 🔒 100% Private Rhythm respects your data. There are no ads, no analytics, and no accounts required. It is completely offline-capable and proudly open-source (GPL v3).

name: Kompanion
short: Remote control companion for KOReader e-readers
description: Kompanion is a remote control companion app for KOReader. It connects over your local network to the HTTP Inspector plugin built into KOReader, letting you control your e-reader from your phone. Features: * Frontlight intensity and warmth control * Night mode toggle * Full screen refresh * Five custom profile buttons that activate one of your KOReader profiles * Page turning with the volume buttons, with remapping capabilities * Navigate back and forward between followed links, with a custom "back" button * Text input screen to get, send, and clear text inside any input widget in KOReader, useful for writing notes from the comfort of your phone * Reading mode: an immersive mode with minimal UI and minimal brightness * Keyboard shortcuts: common keyboards are supported, so you can use this app as a "bridge" for most PowerPoint presenter sticks * Battery information: fetches the current battery capacity and creates a graph for the current session Setup: 1. Install and open KOReader on your e-reader 2. Go to Tools -> More Tools -> KOReader HTTP Inspector and start the HTTP server (note the port, 8080 by default) 3. Go to Settings -> Network -> Network info and note the device's IP address 4. In Kompanion, enter the IP and port and press "Connect" This app requires KOReader's HTTP Inspector plugin to be running on the same local network; it does not talk to any server outside your network.

name: Circadian Display
short: Adaptive screen warmth and dimming curves for better evening comfort and sleep.
description: Circadian Display continuously adjusts your screen's warmth and brightness throughout the evening based on customizable curves you define. Unlike standard night light solutions with fixed on/off schedules, Circadian Display provides a smooth, gradual transition tailored to your preferences. Features: - Dynamic comfort curves with precise warmth and dimming levels over time - Dual-engine modes: Native (system-level, Android 10+ with ADB setup) and Overlay (software-based, works on all devices) - Background scheduler for automatic, hands-free operation - Privacy-first: completely offline, tracker-free, no data collection - Open source (Apache 2.0)

name: Lux Alarm
short: Wake up with light! This alarm can only be turned off when your room is bright
description: Stop Oversleeping with Lux Alarm Tired of hitting snooze and waking up late? Lux Alarm ensures you actually get out of bed by requiring light to silence the alarm. How it works To stop the alarm, you must get up and open your blinds or turn on the light. The app uses your phone's sensor to detect brightness; by the time the alarm turns off, you are already on your feet and ready to start your day. Key Features • Smart Light Detection: Uses your phone's sensor to ensure the alarm only deactivates once your environment is bright. • Adjustable Sensitivity: Customize the required light level to account for gloomy weather or different room setups. • Modern Interface: A clean, intuitive design based on Material Design 3 for easy navigation. • Circadian Support: Waking up with light helps regulate your natural sleep cycle and reduces morning grogginess.

name: Solid Share
short: Files, contacts and passes on your own Solid pod, shared on your terms
description: Solid Share brings the Solid ecosystem to everyday Android users. Sign in with your Solid pod and use it as a personal data wallet: browse your files, keep your address book and your passes on it, share any of it with the people you choose, and let other Solid apps reach it on terms you set. Solid is an open web standard for personal data stores, called pods. Your pod is yours — pick a provider or run your own. Solid Share has no server: the app talks to your pod directly, and nothing you store passes through us. HOME * What changed while you were away: unread notifications, access requests, and the files you opened or that changed * Your next pass, what you shared, and what has been shared with you, on one screen * It tells you when you are offline, and how many changes are waiting to upload FILES * Browse containers and resources in list or grid, sorted by name, type or date * Upload from device storage, or capture a photo or video and upload it straight away * Images, PDFs and text open inside the app; anything else opens with the app of your choice * Share any file from any app straight into your pod, one at a time or many at once * Duplicate a file or folder as a private copy, reset to owner-only access SHARING * Grant a specific Solid user, by WebID, or anyone with the link, access to any file or folder * View, Add and Edit access levels instead of raw Read, Append and Write * Every share produces a QR code and a link that opens straight back into the app * Two pod-backed lists: what you have shared, and what has been shared with you * Widen, narrow or revoke a share at any time; the recipient is told when their access changes * Ask an owner for access when a resource denies you, and answer requests yourself * Works across Solid servers, using Web Access Control with an Access Control Policy fallback APPS ON YOUR PHONE * Other Solid apps reach your pod through Solid Share, so no other app holds your credentials * You decide what each app may do — View, Add, Edit or Full access — and where: your whole pod, folders you choose, or just your contacts * An Apps tab lists every app that has access, and narrows or removes it whenever you like * Grants stay on your device and are never written to your pod WALLET * Event tickets, boarding passes, cinema tickets, loyalty cards and coupons, as ordinary Solid resources you own * Apple Wallet .pkpass import, read in full, with the original file kept beside the ticket * Barcodes re-rendered in the issuer's own sym

name: FreeFTP
short: Free FTP, FTPS and SFTP client. No ads, no paid tier, no tracking.
description: FreeFTP connects your phone to your own servers over FTP, FTPS and SFTP. It is free in both senses: no advertising, no paid tier, no analytics, and no account. The app talks to your servers and to nothing else. It holds one network permission, and the only host it ever contacts is the one you typed in. Features * FTP, FTPS (explicit and implicit) and SFTP in a single client. * Browse, download, upload, rename, delete and create folders. * Read files without downloading them. Tap any text file and it is streamed straight into memory, with nothing written to your storage. The encoding is detected and shown, so you can tell real content from mojibake. * Download whole folders, recursively, with their structure preserved. * Multi-select: long-press to start, then download or delete in bulk. Large jobs ask for confirmation first, and deleting always asks. * A transfer queue with live progress, pause, resume, cancel and retry. A paused transfer keeps what it has and continues from that point. * Downloads land in your Downloads folder, where you can actually find them, or in any folder you choose. No storage permission is requested: you grant access to the one folder you pick. Security * SSH host keys are checked. An unrecognised server is refused until you have seen its SHA-256 fingerprint and accepted it, and a key that later changes is refused outright. * TLS certificates are verified for FTPS, with an explicit opt-in for self-signed ones. * Passwords, key passphrases and private keys are encrypted at rest with a key held in the Android key store. * Password, SSH key (with passphrase) and anonymous authentication, falling back automatically across publickey, password and keyboard-interactive. FreeFTP handles the awkward parts of real-world FTP: passive and active mode, MLSD with a LIST fallback, a dozen server listing dialects, UTF-8 negotiation, and resuming an interrupted transfer.

name: Feedora
short: A modern and elegant RSS reader with Material You design
description: Feedora A modern and elegant RSS reader with Material You Design Features: * Subscribe to feed links * Import from OPML * Article sync * Article update notification * Parse full content * Filter unread and starred * Feed grouping * Localization * Export as OPML * Search for articles More to come…

name: Gluco Glance
short: Read your CGM sensor over Bluetooth. Offline, no accounts, no tracking.
description: Gluco Glance reads your glucose level straight off a CGM sensor over Bluetooth and shows it: the current number, which way it is heading, and a graph you can scrub through. NOT A MEDICAL DEVICE. It is not approved by any regulator and has had no clinical testing. A reading here can be wrong, late, or missing. Do not treat a high or a low on the strength of this app alone. Check with your meter, and follow the advice of whoever looks after your diabetes. SENSORS Sibionics GS1, found on its own with nothing to pair. Abbott FreeStyle Libre 2 and 2 Plus, European models, paired with one NFC tap. You can run several at once, and every sensor you have worn keeps its own colour and its own line on the graph. WHAT IT DOES Dashboard with the reading, the trend, how long the sensor has left, and a graph you can pinch between 3, 6, 12 and 24 hours. Daily Log for meals, notes and moods, each carrying what the sensor said at that moment. Calibration from a fingerprick, so readings slide between pricks as the sensor drifts. Alerts, where a low breaks through a silenced phone and a high does not. A home screen widget and a permanent notification, so you do not have to open the app to use it. PRIVACY The app has no INTERNET permission, so it cannot send your data anywhere. Android enforces that, you do not have to take my word for it. No cloud backup, no analytics, no crash reporting, no adverts, no accounts. It ships with no third-party libraries at all. Sibionics, FreeStyle and Libre are trademarks of their owners. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sibionics or Abbott.

name: Amethyst
short: Nostr Client for Android
description: Amethyst brings the best social network to your Android phone. Just insert your Nostr private key and start posting. Nostr is an open protocol that is able to create a censorship-resistant global "social" network, transferring notes and other stuff using relays. It doesn't rely on any trusted central server, hence it is resilient; it is based on cryptographic keys and signatures, so it is tamperproof; it does not rely on P2P techniques, therefore it works. What you can do with Amethyst Post text, photos, videos, long-form articles, polls and voice notes to the relays you choose. Follow people, reply, repost, react and quote. Send private, end-to-end encrypted direct messages and join group chats. Browse dedicated feeds: articles, pictures, short videos, live streams, podcasts, music, communities, classifieds, calendars and more. Send and receive Bitcoin Lightning zaps. Track your training and share a workout — see below. My Fitness — track your training Amethyst includes a personal training dashboard. Open the left drawer and tap My Fitness , under You . It summarises the workouts you have logged in Amethyst, and — with your permission — the ones your watch or fitness app has already saved to Android Health Connect (Samsung Health, Google Fit, Fitbit, Garmin Connect, Strava and others all write there). It shows you: How much you trained this week, and whether that is up or down on last week. Your four-week weekly average for time, distance, steps and climb. Where your time goes — running, cycling, walking, hiking, swimming, rowing, the gym. Your best efforts: longest distance, longest workout, biggest climb, most steps, highest heart rate. How many days you trained, and your current streak of consecutive active days. All of it is computed on your phone and shown to you. Nothing is uploaded to produce it, and you never have to post anything to use it. Sharing a workout (optional) If you want to tell your followers about a particular session, tap Share this workout on any row. Amethyst opens a post pre-filled with that workout's figures; you review it and decide whether to publish. One workout at a time, always with your confirmation, never automatic. The Health Connect integration is read-only. Amethyst never writes to Health Connect, never reads in the background, never asks for your exercise route or location, and only ever looks at the last four weeks. You can revoke access in Health Connect at any time. Full details are in

name: MediLog (Non-reproducible build)
short: Log health metrics such as blood pressure, weight and quite a few others
description: Privacy respecting logging of blood pressure, oxygen, glucose, temperature, weight, fluid intake, as well as a simple diary. Includes ways to securely share the sensitive data with medical staff if and when required. * Support for biometric(fingerprint) logon * Charts with trends and thresholds * CSV Data export via protected/encrypted zip files * Ability to share health data via PDF files inside protected/encrypted zip files

name: MediLog (Reproducible build)
short: Log health metrics such as blood pressure, weight and quite a few others
description: Privacy respecting logging of blood pressure, oxygen, glucose, temperature, weight, fluid intake, as well as a simple diary. Includes ways to securely share the sensitive data with medical staff if and when required. * Support for biometric(fingerprint) logon * Charts with trends and thresholds * CSV Data export via protected/encrypted zip files * Ability to share health data via PDF files inside protected/encrypted zip files

name: AntennaPod - Podcast Player
short: Easy-to-use, flexible and open-source podcast manager and player
description: AntennaPod is a podcast manager and player that gives you instant access to millions of free and paid podcasts, from independent podcasters to large publishing houses such as the BBC, NPR and CNN. Add, import and export their feeds hassle-free using the Apple Podcasts database, OPML files or simple RSS URLs. Download, stream or queue episodes and enjoy them the way you like with adjustable playback speeds, chapter support and a sleep timer. Save effort, battery power and mobile data usage with powerful automation controls for downloading episodes (specify times, intervals and WiFi networks) and deleting episodes (based on your favourites and delay settings). Made by podcast-enthusiasts, AntennaPod is free in all senses of the word: open source, no costs, no ads. Import, organize and play • Manage playback from anywhere: homescreen widget, system notification and earplug and bluetooth controls • Add and import feeds via the Apple Podcasts, gPodder.net, fyyd or Podcast Index directories, OPML files and RSS or Atom links • Enjoy listening your way with adjustable playback speed, chapter support, remembered playback position and an advanced sleep timer (shake to reset, lower volume) • Access password-protected feeds and episodes Keep track, share & appreciate • Keep track of the best of the best by marking episodes as favourites • Find that one episode through the playback history or by searching titles and shownotes • Share episodes and feeds through advanced social media and email options, the gPodder.net services and via OPML export Control the system • Take control over automated downloading: choose feeds, exclude mobile networks, select specific WiFi networks, require the phone to be charging and set times or intervals • Manage storage by setting the amount of cached episodes, smart deletion and selecting your preferred location • Adapt to your environment using the light and dark theme • Back-up your subscriptions with the gPodder.net integration and OPML export Join the AntennaPod community! AntennaPod is under active development by volunteers. You can contribute too, with code or with comment! Our friendly forum members are happy to help with every question you have. You are invited to discuss features and podcasting in general, too. https://forum.antennapod.org/ AntennaPod is translated on Weblate by volunteers like you: https://hosted.weblate.org/engage/antennapod

name: FMD
short: Locate and control your device remotely
description: I lost my new phone. And because I don't use Google Services I couldn't locate it and my phone was gone for good. In the hope that this doesn't happen again, I developed this application, so that I can locate the phone via SMS. Features: - Locate the device (using GPS or cellular location) - Lock the device - Let the device ring - Take pictures with the device's camera to see its surroundings - Factory-reset the device Usage: You can control FMD (and thus your phone) either via SMS or via FMD Server. You send a command to the phone (e.g. "fmd ring") and the phone executes it. For SMS you can either define a list of trusted contacts (phone numbers) that are allowed to send commands. Or you can set a PIN to allow anonymous usage. Then non-trusted phone numbers can also send commands by including the PIN in the message. This is useful because now if you lose your phone, you can ask a random person for help to wipe your phone remotely. If you simply text "fmd" to your phone FMD will reply with a text listing the available commands. With FMD Server you get a web interface to send commands, to view the location of your device on a map, and to view pictures taken by the device. You can self-host FMD Server. For more details, see: https://gitlab.com/fmd-foss/fmd-server Disclaimer: This app is provided on a best effort basis. We hope it is useful, we use it ourselves, but this is a hobby project and we can't guarantee that it will work when you need it the most.

name: FMD edge
short: Locate and control your device remotely
description: FMD edge is the "cutting edge" version of FMD. FMD edge receives updates faster, more often, and slightly earlier than FMD. FMD edge releases are generally stable and ready for day-to-day use. FMD allows you to locate and remotely control your Android device. This is useful if you have lost or misplaced it. FMD is decentralised, and users remain in full control of their data. For more details about FMD, see the project website (https://fmd-foss.org/docs/overview) or the F-Droid listing for the main FMD app (https://f-droid.org/packages/de.nulide.findmydevice/).

name: OpenStop
short: The app for collecting barrier data in local public transport.
description: The goal of the app is, with your help, to collect public transport barrier data and make it available on OpenStreetMap so that EVERYONE can benefit from it. By asking simple questions about stops, citizens shall be put in a position to collect data in their vicinity in an accessible manner. The data you collect will build the foundation for better travel information, especially for physically impaired people, and guide the upgrading process of bus stops. Thank you for your contribution to a better local public transport.

name: Helio
short: Music sequencer, designed to be used on all major platforms
description: Helio is a libre music sequencer aimed at hobbyist composers, game developers, and indie artists. Follow the documentation to get started: https://docs.helio.fm

name: Epoch
short: Time display for nerds: Unix, sidereal, binary clocks & more.
description: Epoch shows the current moment across a wide range of time systems — updating every second, all in one place. What Epoch gives you - Civil: date, time, day second, day percent, seven-segment clock — for any timezone - Technical: Unix time, International Atomic Time (TAI), GPS time - Astronomical: Greenwich and Local Mean Sidereal Time (GMST, LMST), Julian Date variants - Curiosities: decimal time, Swatch Internet Time, New Earth Time, Doomsday Clock, 3 binary clocks, octal time and hexadecimal time Copy any value to clipboard with one tap or long press. Configurable - Build your own Watchlist tabs — combine any value from any category, in any order. - All built-in tabs (Civil, Technical, Astronomical, Curiosities) are fully customizable too, and can be hidden and restored anytime. - Set custom labels, section headers, and dividers. - Reorder by drag-and-drop, swipe to remove. - Customize date and time formats, configure timezone information. - Optionally pin timezones to always show standard or summer time. - 7-day advance notice of clock changes, with upcoming transitions shown in the value's info dialog. - Export, import, and reset all preferences. Focus mode - Double-tap any value for a full-screen, always-on display — ideal as a bedside clock. - Adjustable brightness (Android) and text color. - Toggle details with a long press. - Burn-in protection through gentle, periodic pixel shifting (especially useful on OLED screens). - Optionally start the app directly in Focus mode. Designed for night use Night mode displays red text on black — preserving your eyes' dark adaptation for stargazing. Example configurations Ready-to-import example configurations are available on GitHub, including spaceflight tab, world timezone explorer, and config manual. Privacy first No ads, notifications, tracking, analytics, or network requests. All settings stored locally on your device. No permissions required. For Local Mean Sidereal Time: optionally grant location access once (coarse, no GPS) or enter longitude manually. Available in English and German.

name: Drausible
short: Read your Plausible Analytics stats, from plausible.io or a self-hosted server
description: Drausible shows your Plausible Analytics stats on your Android phone. Add the server, whether that is plausible.io cloud or a Community Edition one you run yourself on your hardware, add the sites you want to observe, and you get the dashboard without opening a browser. No account, you issue the API key which you feed to the application. You need to add sites manually, as site listing is not a part of Community Edition API. Stats per site: * Visitors, visits, pageviews, views per visit, bounce rate and average visit duration * Visitors over time chart, bucketed by the hour when you look at a single day * Top pages, sources, countries, devices with a switch between type, browser and OS * How many visitors are on the site right now, kept up to date while the screen is open A few things that matter if you self-host: * Servers too old for the v2 stats API will fall back to v1 automatically * Plain HTTP works too, as instances on a home network often run without TLS * Each server can go through its own SOCKS5 proxy, so a .onion address works with Orbot

name: API Flow
short: A focused mobile workspace for testing HTTP APIs
description: API Flow is a compact mobile API client for testing HTTP endpoints without a desktop. • Send GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS requests • Add headers, query parameters, and raw request bodies • Inspect response status, timing, headers, and body • Save local request collections and recent history • Use a reusable {{base_url}} environment variable • Choose light, dark, or system appearance API Flow has no accounts, ads, analytics, or developer-operated backend. Requests are only sent when you choose an endpoint and tap Send.

name: Shellwave
short: An SSH client that doesn't make you choose between convenient and trustworthy
description: Shellwave is an SSH client for Android phones and foldables, built because every mobile SSH client makes you choose between convenient and trustworthy — and that's a stupid choice. Sessions that survive Your train goes into a tunnel and the connection drops. When the signal comes back, your session is still there — reconnected without re-typing a password, and with optional tmux-backed sessions, reattached with scrollback intact. You don't do anything. Hosts can also keep a persistent session running, so you can close the app and come back to exactly where you left off. Nothing is trusted for you Host keys are checked the first time you connect and remembered after that, with the fingerprint shown so you can check it yourself. If a host key ever changes, Shellwave stops you before you go any further. There is no accept-all mode, and a script running from a widget or a tile never answers a prompt on your behalf. Your keys stay on your device Password, an imported private key, a key generated on your device, or keyboard-interactive/2FA — whatever you already use. Everything is encrypted on-device, with hardware-backed protection on phones that support it, and an optional biometric lock. You can generate a key on the device and install it in a host's authorized_keys without the private key ever leaving the phone. Save yourself the typing Save commands or scripts against a host, with parameters you fill in when you run them. Watch them run live, run them in the background and check back later, or fire them into a session you already have open. You can launch a script from the app itself, a home-screen widget, an app shortcut, or a Quick Settings tile. Networking, done properly - Local and remote port forwarding - A SOCKS5 proxy - Jump host/bastion chaining through multiple hops - Import your existing ~/.ssh/config as-is — hosts, ports, users, keys, jump hosts Forwarded ports and the proxy bind to loopback unless you say otherwise. File transfer Send files to a host or pull them down over SFTP, without switching apps. A real terminal 256 colours, wide character support, correct cursor and scroll handling. If you use vim, tmux, or htop, they will look and behave the way you expect. No weird redraws, no broken keys, no compromises. Built with foldables in mind On unfolded or wide screens you get a two-pane layout, host list next to the terminal. Tabletop mode keeps the terminal above the hinge and the keyboard below it. Fold or unfold mid-session and nothing drop

name: SkyPulse
short: Decode and monitor 1090 MHz ADS-B aircraft with an RTL-SDR
description: SkyPulse is an Android receiver for monitoring 1090 MHz Mode S and ADS-B traffic with an RTL-SDR. It decodes aircraft data on-device using the separate FLOSS marto.rtl_tcp_andro driver, displays aircraft on a map, and includes offline FIR and TRACON boundary data. The map uses OpenFreeMap when opened, and boundary updates are optional. For unattended stations, boot startup is user-configurable. Beast TCP output is optional, disabled by default, and limited to localhost for local tools such as readsb. SkyPulse has no analytics, advertising, or account requirement, and does not depend on Google Play Services.

name: Hestia
short: Local control of Shelly devices — no cloud, no account, no tracking.
description: Hestia controls your Shelly smart-home devices (Gen2 and later) directly on your local network, over HTTP, through their built-in API. No cloud, no account, no telemetry: nothing leaves your network, by default. Features: * Channel dashboard with state and switch, at a glance. * "On for X" timer executed by the device itself, fully autonomously (the phone can be turned off). * Presence simulation: a script generated by the app runs on the device and switches on/off within a time window, with a random margin. * Planning (recurring or one-time), with an optional power-threshold cutoff. * Backup and restore of your configuration in JSON format. * Optional instant notifications via ntfy (off by default). Privacy: * Communicates only with the addresses you enter yourself. * No network discovery, no tracking. * On Android 17 and later, the local network access permission is requested on first contact, preceded by a clear explanation. Language: the app is available in French and English, and follows the system language (English by default, French if the device is set to French). Independence: Hestia is an independent project, with no connection to Shelly or Allterco Robotics. It is neither commissioned, sponsored, nor endorsed by Shelly. No payment and no hardware were provided or lent by the brand. Shelly is a registered trademark of its respective owner; it is mentioned only for technical compatibility.

name: RPClient
short: AI roleplay chat and story writing client
description: RPClient is an AI roleplay and storytelling client with support for common tavern-style character cards and lorebooks. Create your own characters, write multi-chapter stories, start one-on-one chats, or build group chats where multiple characters join the same story. RPClient is not an Android remake of SillyTavern. It is a mobile-focused roleplay and storytelling app that supports familiar workflows such as character cards, lorebooks, prompts, and long-term story memory, while offering an interface designed for Android. Key features: - Write and organize multi-chapter stories with Story Studio (volumes, chapters, and continuation prompts) - View model reasoning and thought processes in real time during generation - Backup and share stories with .rpstory archive export and import - Import JSON and PNG character cards (including batch import) - Create, edit, and manage your own characters - Import and manage tavern-style lorebooks (with mutual exclusion groups) - Start one-on-one AI character chats - Create group chats with multiple characters - Regenerate, continue, or stop replies - Generate from the user’s perspective - Keep long stories going with summary memory - Assign independent models to specific characters and summaries - Import and export chat histories compatible with SillyTavern (.jsonl) - Manage prompts, character settings, greetings, and story context - Connect to OpenAI-compatible APIs, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, and custom providers - Chats, stories, characters, and settings are stored on your device by default RPClient does not include a built-in AI model service. To chat or generate stories, you need to configure your own model provider or API key. Requests are sent to the provider you choose, so please use services you trust. RPClient is not an official SillyTavern Android app and is not affiliated with OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, DeepSeek, or OpenRouter.

name: Productivity System - timeto.me
short: Goals, checklists, tasks, repetitive tasks, calendar and 24/7 time tracking.
description: I built this app to manage my productivity. Here, I will SHARE my productivity system and how I use the app. My system IS ALL ABOUT achieving my REAL-LIFE goals. For example: - I DO NOT care how much time I waste, - but I CARE if I read a book every day, - I CARE if I exercise every day, - I CARE if I don't forget anything, - I CARE if I constantly follow my long-term goals. Now I will show MY PERSONAL app setup with REAL-LIFE scenarios. --- Activities The first you have to do is SET UP ACTIVITIES. MY ACTIVITIES in the morning, right after I wake up look empty. During the day, I have to turn them as completed. Now I'll show how I use each activity. --- Morning Right after waking up, I tap the Morning activity. Once I finish the checklist, Morning will be marked as complete. --- Workout I DO NOT care about tracking every single step, but I CARE I do workout every day. --- Small Tasks We all have plenty of non-urgent tasks that we constantly postpone. Every day, I FORCE MYSELF to spend 30 minutes for that. --- Work Working as a developer, I have to track my working hours, there are a set of features for that. Total Stopwatch makes the timer display TOTAL TIME spent on work FOR TODAY. This way, I can always see how much time I've spent on work today. Another feature is adding notes to the current task. You can see how much time you spent on each task. I use a POMODORO-LIKE technique. --- Reading Some people set a goal to read for a hour a day. I like to read a fixed number of chapters per day. It works like a counter. --- Free Time I use Free Time for activities I don't need to track, like eating, walking, meeting, etc. --- Sleep I prefer to use a stopwatch to check in the morning how long I slept. --- Conclusion By default, the app comes with almost the same activities and settings. You can use this setup. I want to give you THREE TIPS dealing with activities that are extremely important to me: PROCRASTINATION, PRIORITIES, and FLEXIBILITY. --- Procrastination I solve it simply: I open the app, see uncompleted activity, and tap on it without thinking. Tapping the activity feels like you've made the first step. If you start thinking, you will continue procrastinating. --- Priorities We usually start the day with the most urgent tasks and SACRIFICE long-term goals, because long-term goals are not usually urgent. NO MATTER what happens, I try to start my day focusing only on what really MATTERS TO ME. --- Flexibility Unexpected things happen every day. We have t

name: AndBible: Bible Study
short: Powerful Bible study toolkit: commentaries, bookmarks, notes, AI tools
description: Powerful Bible Study tool "AndBible: Bible Study" is a powerful, easy-to-use, offline Bible study app for Android — a versatile toolkit of high-quality features serving many study styles, from casual reading to in-depth research. More than a reader, it's a tool for serious personal study. Developed by Bible readers, for Bible readers — a non-profit, open-source community project that is completely free and contains no ads. Many popular Bible versions are available including KJV, NASB, NET, and others. Popular commentaries like Matthew Henry and John Gill are also available. Powerful Bible Study features The application has many insightful and original features that makes a complex and deep Bible study experience smoother than ever. The most notable features are: * Split text views that enable comparing translations and consulting commentaries * Workspaces allow multiple Bible study setups with their own settings * Strong's integration allows Greek and Hebrew word analysis * Tap any link to follow hyperlinked cross-references, footnotes, and commentaries (Gill, Matthew Henry etc.) or cross-reference collections (Treasure of Scripture Knowledge, TSKe). * Optional AI study agent (opt-in only — requires your own API key for an external service): explore your installed commentaries and dictionaries with AI assistance in your chosen language, plus other creative study workflows. A built-in permission system keeps you in full control of what the agent can do. * Flexible full-text search across one or many Bible translations simultaneously * Advanced bookmarking & highlighting features with personal study notes * Study Pads for adding notes and Bible references while listening to sermons * Reading and memorization tracking: set reading goals, track progress, and memorize verses with interactive Word Scramble, Word Order, Word Blur, and Type It modes * Advanced text to speech with speak bookmarks, enabling a smooth Bible listening experience * Cross-device sync: keep your workspaces, bookmarks, notes, and reading progress in sync across all your devices * Vast library of documents: Bible translations, theological commentaries, dictionaries, maps, and christian books, totaling over 1500 documents in over 700 languages, legally distributed by Crosswire and other SWORD repositories * Native support for MyBible, MySword and EPUB files enables you to extend your library even more Let’s make the best Bible app together! AndBible is an open-source community project. In pr

name: Casio G-Shock Smart Sync
short: Add smart functions to your Casio square BT G-Shock Watch.
description: G-Shock Smart Sync is an unofficial, open-source Android app for G-Shock, Edifice, and Pro Trek watches. It allows you to control your watch, sync data, and configure settings without a Casio ID. It offers a faster, privacy-focused, and more powerful alternative to the official Casio app. Key Features: - No Account Required: Skip the Casio ID login entirely. - Calendar Sync: Push your calendar events (Google, Samsung, etc.) to your watch as reminders. - Auto Timezone: Automatically adjusts watch time when you travel. - Remote Control: Use your watch buttons to take photos, control music, or launch voice assistants. - Alarm Sync: Configure watch alarms easily from your phone. - Phone Finder: Trigger a loud alarm on your phone to find it. Supported Watch Models: The app works with many Bluetooth-enabled G-Shock, Edifice, and Pro Trek models. - Square: GW-B5600, GMW-B5000, GW-B5000, DW-B5600, TRN-50 - CasiOak: GA-B2100, GBM-2100, GMC-B2100, MRG-B2100 - G-Steel: GST-B100 to B1000, GST-W1000, ECB-900 - Edifice: ECB-10 to ECB-2300, EQB-500 to EQB-2000 - MT-G / MR-G: MTG-B1000/B3000/B3100, MRG-B5000/B2100 - Others: ABL-100WE, GBD-100/200, GBD-H1000/H2000, GPR-B1000 Note: While these watches connect, not all specific hardware features may be fully supported yet. App Walkthrough: 1. Connection Screen: Handles the Bluetooth connection via BLE. Connection is typically much faster than the official app (~3.5s vs 12s). 2. Time Setting: Manage your watch's timekeeping effortlessly. Sync your phone's time, timezone, and DST settings to the watch immediately. 3. Alarms: Read and configure the 5 alarms stored on your watch and the hourly signal (Chime). 4. Events (Calendar Sync): Sync your Android calendars to your watch! Pushes events to the watch's Reminder feature. 5. Actions (Remote Control): Turn your watch into a remote control. Assign actions to button presses (Find Phone, Take Photo, Flashlight, Next Track, Voice Assist, Set Prayer Alarms). 6. Settings: Configure app and watch preferences like light duration, power saving, and more. Related Projects: - G-Shock Time Server: Headless time server for Raspberry Pi or Linux. - G-Shock API for ESP32: Standalone time server firmware for ESP32. - G-Shock Smart Sync Webapp: Browser-based synchronization via Web Bluetooth. - GShockAPI: The core library this app is built on.

name: SMSecure
short: Privacy-focused SMS app with encrypted conversations
description: 💬 SMSecure is a privacy-focused SMS messenger for Android. SMSecure is a fork of Silence/TextSecure, created to preserve encrypted SMS functionality on modern Android devices. It keeps the familiar feel of a classic SMS app while adding tools for private, verified conversations. 🔐 Encrypted SMS conversations Use end-to-end encrypted SMS with compatible contacts. SMSecure uses the Signal encryption protocol for secure conversations when both sides support it. 🛡️ Identity verification Verify contacts using QR codes or safety numbers to help protect against man-in-the-middle attacks. 📱 Works as a normal SMS app Send and receive regular SMS messages without creating an account, signing in, or depending on a central messaging service. 🚫 Block unwanted messages Block unwanted senders, including unknown or alphanumeric SMS senders, and keep your inbox cleaner. 🔎 Search your conversations Quickly find messages across all conversations with global search. 💾 Backups and restore Create and restore message backups so you can keep your SMS history under your control. 🌍 Local-first privacy Messages are processed on your device. SMSecure does not require registration, does not use ads, and does not collect user data. ⚠️ Important note End-to-end encryption works only when both sides use compatible software. Regular SMS messages are still regular SMS and are handled by the mobile network. 🧩 Free and Open Source SMSecure is Free and Open Source Software licensed under GPLv3. The source code is available for review, auditing, and contribution. Open-Source Code: https://github.com/jimvixx/ShortMessageSecure

name: LibreFit
short: Free, open source and private workout tracker with a rich dataset and images.
description: LibreFit is a free and open-source workout tracker designed with privacy in mind. Create fully personalized workouts assembled from a rich dataset of hundreds of exercises — each exercise paired with images and step-by-step instructions covering setup and execution. Schedule single sessions, filter exercises by equipment, muscle group or difficulty with one tap. name: Escapepod - Podcast Player
short: Escapepod is a simple and lightweight app for listening to podcasts.
description: Escapepod is a straightforward and lightweight app that takes a minimalistic approach to podcast listening, which may not appeal to everyone. The app consists of only two screens: a list of all podcasts and a list of episodes for a single podcast. Escapepod lacks a podcast discovery feature, offering only a simple search option. Additionally, it opens RSS podcast links when tapped in a web browser. VERIFY APK ---------- APKs published on Codeberg Releases are signed with the following certificate. SHA-256: 61:05:14:5F:84:E5:CB:D6:97:F0:F6:E1:2C:97:77:04:2E:9B:2D:B6:67:A7:FF:0D:A4:12:F6:74:35:31:6D:D8 FREQUENT QUESTIONS ------------------ DOES ESCAPEPOD HAVE PLAYBACK QUEUE? Escapepod has a simple up-next feature. Tap play on an episode while listening to another one. You will be be given the opportunity add it to the up-next slot. WHAT ARE THE DEFAULT SETTINGS? - Auto-update does not download files over cellular network - Escapepod by default only keeps two episodes CAN ESCAPEPOD KEEPS MORE THAN TWO EPISODES? Escapepod tries to reduce the number of episodes it keeps. Here are the rules for that: - Escapepod keeps the latest two episodes - Episodes, that have been started, or that have been downloaded manually, are kept, too - Episodes that have not been listened to in more than two weeks are removed. DOES ESCAPEPOD SUPPORT OPML? You can import a podcast list using the OPML exchange format using the respective option in the app's Settings. The current podcast collection can be exported via Settings, too. Additionally Escapepod keeps an up-to-date OPML file in the folder /Android/data/org.y20k.escapepod/files/collection/. WHERE DO THE PODCAST SEARCH RESULTS COME FROM? Escapepod searches by default the Podcastindex.org (https://podcastindex.org/) online database - or if you toggle the respective setting the gpodder.net (https://gpodder.net/directory/) online database.

name: Transistor - Simple Radio App

WHERE DO THE RADIO STATION SEARCH RESULTS COME FROM? Transistor searches the radio-browser.info online database. You can help out the radio-browser.info community by adding the missing station (http://www.radio-browser.info/gui/#!/add) to their database. HOW CAN I CURATE THE RADIO STATION LIST? Use the swipe gesture to delete a radio station from the list. Further editing options can be enabled in Settings. If enabled, tap and hold a radio station to edit its name, image or streaming link.

Self-Custody Zodl puts you in complete control of your funds: no gatekeepers, no middlemen, just true financial sovereignty. Only you can access and manage your ZEC. Your keys, your crypto. name: Huda
short: Prayer times, Quran, Qibla, Tasbih, Adhkar and more — your Islamic companion
description: Huda is a comprehensive Islamic companion app designed to support your daily worship and spiritual growth. It brings the tools Muslims need most into one clean, ad-free experience. Features: * Quran: complete Mushaf in authentic Uthmanic script, translations and Tafsir, audio recitations with offline playback, and smart reading-position tracking. * Prayer Times & Adhan: accurate location-based prayer times with multiple calculation methods, Adhan notifications and countdown timers. * Qibla Compass: precise Qibla direction with smooth animations and haptic feedback. * Digital Tasbih: a persistent Dhikr counter with notes and tracking. * Athkar & Duas: categorized daily supplications with audio pronunciation. * Daily Checklist: track prayers and habits, build streaks, with Hijri calendar integration. * Hadith & Islamic Library: curated books and Hadith collections with a built-in offline PDF reader. * Home Screen Widgets: quick access to prayer times and core features. * Miqaat Lock: optionally block selected distracting apps during prayer times or custom time slots. On Android, Huda requests Accessibility and display-over-other-apps access only when you choose to enable this feature. * Multilingual & Themes: full RTL Arabic support, dynamic language switching, and Dark/Light themes. Note: some features (such as content sync and the AI assistant) rely on a remote server to work. The FOSS edition asks for your permission before automatically sending crash details, device model, manufacturer, Android version and app version to Huda's Supabase service. You can change this choice later in Settings.

name: MESH
short: Censorship-resisting overlay network for digital forensics
description: MESH is a censorship-resisting, peer-to-peer first, end-to-end encrypted overlay network for digital forensics. It's a fork of the Tailscale protocol, but is self-hostable and heavily modified for civil society and forensic operations.

name: Saracroche
short: Block unwanted spam calls and SMS, and protect your privacy
description: Note: This application is intended for use in France only. Saracroche is an Android app that protects you from unwanted calls by automatically blocking spam phone calls. It's designed to be simple, effective, and privacy-friendly. Features: • Automatically blocks spam numbers • Hides SMS notifications from spam numbers • Blocks anonymous (hidden) calls • "Contacts only" mode: only allows calls from your contacts • Personal lists: create your own block and allow lists • Wildcard patterns: use # as a trailing wildcard (e.g. 33162######) to block a range of numbers • Blocked call log: view the history of filtered calls • Report a number: help improve community blocklists • Reverse directory: look up information about a number on saracroche.org • Native Android application • Available in French, English, German, Spanish, and Italian Privacy & Security: Saracroche prioritizes your privacy. The app operates locally on your device and doesn't collect any personal information or call data. All spam detection is performed on-device using a regularly updated database. How it works: The app uses Android's Call Screening Service to automatically identify and block known spam numbers before they can disturb you. When a call comes in, Saracroche checks the number against its spam database and blocks it if it's identified as spam. Lists are automatically updated every 24 hours and downloaded from saracroche.org. Requirements: • Android 10 (API level 29) or higher • Permission to be set as the default caller ID & spam blocking app for call screening • Intended for use in France only Open Source: Saracroche is open source software under the GPLv3 license. You can review the code, contribute, or build it yourself from the source code available on Codeberg.

name: C2K — Couch to 5K & 10K
short: Offline C25K & C210K trainer with voice coaching. No ads, no tracking.
description: C2K is an offline running trainer that guides you from the couch to running 5K, 10K, and beyond. Follow a clear plan, hear hands-free coaching, and keep your progress private — with no ads and no tracking. Programs: • Pre-C25K — 3-week gentle starter for absolute beginners • Couch to 5K (C25K) — 9-week program, 3 runs per week • Bridge to 10K (B210K) — 6-week bridge for C25K graduates • Couch to 10K (C210K) — 14-week program, continues from C25K • One Hour Runner — 13-week progression from 30 to 60 minutes continuous running • 5K Improver — 8-week speed and stamina program for runners who can already complete 5K Features: • Audible voice prompts — "Start running", "Walk for 90 seconds", countdown warnings • Customizable coaching — adjust voice speed/volume, countdown warning timing, and mid-interval cues • Test voice playback before a workout, with Android text-to-speech diagnostics • Vibration cues as an alternative or addition to voice • Adjustable vibration strength and language selection • Background workout timer — continues with screen off • GPS tracking (optional) — records distance and pace; works without GPS too • Treadmill mode — indoor runs without GPS • Workout history — session log with total distance, time, best pace, longest run, and calorie estimates • Progress tracking — remembers which weeks and days you've completed, with the option to reset • In-app running guide — FAQ covering pacing, gear, and terminology • Available in 8 languages — English, German, Spanish, French, Galician, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Turkish • Works offline — no internet permission required • No proprietary services required — compatible with GrapheneOS and privacy-focused devices Permissions: • FOREGROUND_SERVICE — keeps the workout timer running with screen off • WAKE_LOCK — prevents the CPU sleeping mid-workout • ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION — optional GPS for distance/pace tracking (you can skip this) • POST_NOTIFICATIONS — workout notification with pause/stop controls • VIBRATE — optional vibration cues during workouts C2K is free software released under the GNU General Public License v3.

name: Nexus Command Center

Features: * Budgets, accounts, net worth, portfolio and live market data * Pulls in workouts from LimeLog and study sessions from StudyDesk * Streak-aware habit tracker * Configurable Life Profiles and goals * Weekly and yearly reviews with heatmaps Local-first with on-device storage; optional account-gated cloud sync. No Google Play Services, no Firebase — Google sign-in is a plain web OAuth flow. Third-party market data and an optional AI feature are user-initiated HTTPS calls.
